=== STORY ===
A lamb, being sacrificed by The Bishops from “The Old Faith” is saved from death by an ancient god-like entity called “The One who waits”. In repayment for his life, The Lamb must become its new prophet, create a cult in its name and get revenge against the bishops who imprisoned it.

=== GAMEPLAY ===
Gameplay can be divided in two main categories: Action roguelike and resource management
As Action roguelike, you have to explore different regions, each one controlled by a bishop, in “crusades” where you’ll have to fight enemies, mini-bosses and bosses, gather resources, gain followers, meet new characters, etc. in randomly generated maps. For this, you’ll always start a region with a main weapon (they can go from light/fast attack to heavy/slow attack) and a special ability called “curse”. The mechanics are very simple, you can attack with your weapon or curse, dodge-roll and other abilities which you can unlock later but not much really. Weapons and curses can have different special effects but not much besides that and can get repetitive after a while. When it comes to enemies, there is some variety but once you have seem them all, you can learn their patterns pretty quick and dispose of them without much of a problem. Mini-bosses and Bosses are the strong element here; they can be challenging and kinda most of the time.
Resource management comes into play when it’s related to your cult. You’ll have base where you’ll start creating your cult. For this, you’ll have to gain followers (usually can be added by crusades or by side-quests) which are necessary to gather devotion points which helps you improve things in your cult and your crusades.  But for this to happen, you have to keep your followers happy. This can be done by improving the living conditions in your cult by creating new buildings (houses, devotion places, decorations, farms, etc.), take care of their demands (think of them as side-quests), keep the place clean (THEY POOP A LOT AT FIRST) and feed them, etc. The main building in your cult will be the Chapel were you can perform a variety of actions that will help you in the way you want to guide your flock. You can perform a daily sermon, rituals, create laws, etc.
The way these two categories interact is that the performance of your cult will determine your progress in your crusades. Devotion points will help you improve your weapons/curses, unlock new areas, etc. So, if you keep a functioning cult, your progress will going without much of a problem.
Speaking of problems though, this “relationship” can get a bit tedious and repetitive after a while. While I still enjoyed to keep my cult in order and the crusades, I think the lack of variety in the mechanics and lack of story elements in the game sometimes made ongoing requirements to keep forward with the game, more than a chore than a fun time.

=== VISUALS & SOUND ===
I think this is the strong point of this game. The mix of cute characters with dark/horror elements work really well imo. Aside from the followers, most NPCs, enemies and bosses have really cool/interesting designs and I enjoyed watching them.
When it comes to sound, sound effects are good in general. Characters don’t talk but the have “talk sounds” which usually are unique for each NPC, which gives certain vibe that goes well with how they look. When it comes to combat, there’s not much variety that I could remember but nothing to complain about that though. When it comes to music, it has some really nice tunes in general. I mostly remember the calm/chill tunes vs the more “serious” ones tbh btu still, nice work on the soundtrack.

=== FINAL THOUGHTS ===
A really mix of cute and horror designs with a mix of action and resource management  that work relatively well most of the time but not without some flaws of being kinda tedious and repetitive at times. Still, it was a fun experience in general, not much for a replay though.

[h1] (NOT ABOUT THE BUGS)[/h1] 

[b] ROUGE-LIKE ELEMENTS / COMBAT: [/b] 
I saw this game being marketed as a rogue-like and being compared to others in the genre. This is by far the weakest element of the game. It is technically a rouge-like as it does have procedurally generated rooms however there aren't many of them and they are designed poorly. You will sometimes take damage immediately after entering a room and the enemy design is very bland. The hitboxes for most attacks are janky and unclear and you will often struggle against the controls to attack in the direction you want (I played on controller, also tried keyboard in demo)

There is almost no player choice when it comes to choosing your build. You are limited to around 5-6 options of base weapons which all function basically the same except they have differing speed and damage stats. Due to the nature of the enemy designs the slow high dmg weapons hammer/axe are by far the best and everything else feels very weak. The game will randomly select one of these for you at the start and you don't really have much opportunity to swap to a different one. I played on the "Hard" difficulty and found the game was either far too easy or moderately challenging/frustrating depending entirely on the weapon. 

Other elements of combat are the curses which are spells that consume fervor (mana). Similarly to the weapons these lack variety but are very low impact and deciding to use them will either get you hit due to the charge times/animations or deal less damage than you would have if you just hit them with your weapon. You will also occasionally get to pick from two cards which give single-run enhancements although you don't have to think much about which to pick since it becomes very clear which ones are OP and which are useless after reading them once and there isn't much opportunity or reason to synergize them.


[b] PROGRESSION SYSTEM: [/b] 
During the tutorial, the game makes a very clear effort to show off all the "content" it has to offer by constantly displaying several locked icons and overwhelming you with new mechanics (which conveniently takes you around 2hrs to complete🤔). Upon further inspection, the main combat skill tree will only allow you to add variations or upgrades to the base weapons/curses with boring on-hit effects (poison/crit) or higher damage and they don't add any variety to the combat. You can also very easily progress through the skill trees way too fast. I had maxed out most of the skill tree at around the midpoint of the story.


[b] BASE BUILDING: [/b] 
Around 80% of the things in the game you can unlock are purely cosmetic. I knew going into it that this game would have some base building and cosmetic stuff but the building tools were janky to use and didn’t offer much room for creativity. The rest of the game is also so short the base will become entirely useless very quickly and you have no reason to visit it or spend time working on it. Most of the non-cosmetic base upgrades provide automation of your chores except you still have to go to each individual building to collect resources, babysit the workers ect. And again, by the time you get most of the automation setup you have no reason to care about/visit the base so it's not satisfying to not have to do it anymore.


[b] COLONY MANAGEMENT:[/b] 
A Lot of the time you spend on managing your colony revolves around running around and pressing the same button over and over again. You're constantly babysitting your colonists, including literally cleaning their shit off the ground. Colonists can be buffed or have innate traits that make them better/worse at certain tasks however they will constantly stop to take a dump on the floor then completely forget what they were doing making the traits another useless feature that provides fake depth. They can however send you on truly exhilarating quests, such as making a colonist eat a bowl of shit 3 times. 

What frustrates me most is that there is no interface for managing your colonists or viewing traits all at once so you will have to constantly run around to check things. The game also makes you spend time running around to interact with each individual colonist every in game day (~10 mins)  in order to level them up and will play the same 3 sec animation each time you do. They also age extremely rapidly and have a life expectancy of around 1-2 IRL hours and you are pressured to sacrifice them which made it even harder for me to want to go through all the tedium of leveling them in the first place since there is almost no reward for doing so. Their expendability and lack of meaningful unique qualities also makes it so there is absolutely no point in using the colonist customization feature so I feel sorry for anyone who bought the colonist skin DLC pack.


[b] POST-GAME/FUTURE CONTENT: [/b] 
There is none. Don't expect any replayability. The devs have stated they plan to release free post-game content and improvements in future. There is a “roadmap” on the title screen however clicking it does not provide details on what's planned to be added. Regardless of whether or not this happens, this game is not listed as early access (though it feels like it is) and I do not believe this should be used to counter any criticism of the product they are currently selling.


[b] CONCLUSION (TL;DR): [/b] 
I do think the devs had good intentions but at the end of the day this just plays like they took a bunch of mechanics from popular games and tried to cram them in the demo/refund window to reach a wide appeal. Compared to the games it draws from, there is a lack of innovation to the mechanics and far less depth to the gameplay. 


[b] [i] My recommendation for someone considering purchasing this game? [/i] 

[u] Don't. [/u] Playing the demo on repeat for 10-15 hours is basically the same experience minus the disappointment.[/b]
